_comment: Scenario-staged rout-then-ANNIHILATION demo: a lone low-morale (1) player infantry block of 12 is charged head-on by two 12-horse cavalry troops and BREAKS -- it enters routing (drawn faded) and flees toward its own back edge. The squadrons are shallow and spawn close so their facing-front is in spatha reach at regiment contact; a deep 80-horse column's front would sit a mounted rank-pitch past the infantry and land no per-soldier blows. Routing units are still valid combat targets, and the cavalry (8.5 sprint) are faster than the fleeing infantry (4.0 sprint), so pursuit is relentless: they catch it, and the casualties from being run down erode its morale faster than it can recover, so it never rallies. It's eventually ANNIHILATED (soldiers reach zero) rather than escaping or rallying. The router now flees at its real flee pace, so the chase is a real run up the lane -- the lead squadron (uid 3) catches it at tick 420, fights it on the move to tick 542, chases it again and cuts it down between ticks 648 and 650 -- and the scene still runs on a custom tall map (field 1600x2400, flat) with every actor staged in the deep south: the flee lane north is ~1800 wu to the retreat margin, giving the kill ~5x the locally measured flight distance of headroom against the slower-platform divergence that let the router ESCAPE the default 1200-tall field on CI. The staging is the original scene translated south by exactly 1200 including the safe spearmen anchor -- the cavalry AI's target scoring sees that anchor's relative position, and moving it (measured) flips the arc from a clean chase to an enveloped kill-in-place with no visible pursuit. A second, safe player unit stays in the fight so the battle doesn't declare defeat and freeze the instant the infantry routs. Deterministic via the seed (rout by tick 60, caught at tick 420, annihilated between ticks 648 and 650, measured with a 2-tick state dump of the catalog clip; it used to crawl and take until ~tick 2640). Camera frames the clash and then pans up the flee lane with the chase, holding on the kill (website/tools/demo-catalog.sh records 360 frames at 30 fps, to tick 720 -- about 1.2 seconds past the kill, so a run-down up to about a second later still lands inside the clip). The expect list pins the lead squadron targeting the router and engaged in melee, and the router gone from play by tick 700. No player input needed. (A unit that truly breaks free instead recovers cleanly -- see test/unit/test_morale_recovery_demo_scenario.gd for that case in isolation.)

shape_residual.reason: The pursuing cavalry troop (uid 3) never routs, so no #1739 code path runs in its own update. The one way #1739 reaches it is through the router: the router's refreshed enemy-contact flag feeds this unit's own _separate() pair test against the router while the two are in contact. On the merge-base it stays in contact with the crawling router, FIGHTING, through the clip, so its samples are never judged. Now the router flees at its real pace: uid 3 catches it at tick 420 and fights it on the move until tick 542, loses contact and chases it MOVING (judged) to tick 626, fights it again, and the router is gone at tick 650. Sustained shape residual on a 2-tick scan from tick 400: 40.83 wu at the #1739 head against 8.678 wu on the merge-base (threshold 30). Tracked as a pursuer deforming on engaging a full-pace router in #1757.
